display.title: Episode 545: The Young Baal Shem Tov in the Cave (Chai Elul)
display.summary_short: On the eve of Chai Elul, the birthday of the Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe, Uncle Yossi tells how the orphan Yisrolik studied alone in a cave and feared nothing but Hashem.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on the eve of Chai Elul 5752. Uncle Yossi explains that the 18th of Elul is the birthday of two great tzaddikim, the Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe. On a birthday a person's mazal is strong, and a tzaddik's soul continues to help Klal Yisrael from Gan Eden, especially on his birthday, so now, at the end of golus, we need their blessings more than ever. After the march, a first-grade class from a Crown Heights cheder leads the Shema, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time tells of little Yisrolik, orphaned at five. On his deathbed his father told him to fear nothing and no one but Hashem. Yisrolik finds an empty cave in the forest and studies there in secret, until a stranger with a silvery beard asks if he is afraid to be alone. 'I'm not alone, Hashem is here,' he answers, and asks the stranger to teach him Torah. The boy grows up to be the Baal Shem Tov. Uncle Yossi then explains the Alter Rebbe's parable of the king in the field: in Elul Hashem is close and accepts every request. The show ends with Tehillim for the Rebbe's recovery, information about enrolling in a yeshiva, candle-lighting time and wishes for a good year.
display.lesson: Fear nothing and no one but Hashem, and you are never alone; in Elul Hashem is close, like a king in the field.

date.note: 'Tonight is the 18th day of the month of Elul': Tuesday 15 September 1992 (17 Elul by day); Friday candle-lighting 6:42 matches 18 September 1992.
